findings.title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock (no double-checked locking)
findings.body: After the RLock fast path fails, the function takes the write lock but never re-reads `entryPointAssetsCache`. If N requests arrive concurrently before the cache is populated (e.g. at startup), all N will block on the write lock and each will in turn re-open and re-parse `assets-manifest.json` (and, when the CDN branch is enabled, perform an HTTP request) and overwrite the cache, even though the first one already populated it. Re-checking `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `Lock()` would make the cache actually serve concurrent callers and avoid the redundant I/O.

findings.title: Blocking file/network I/O performed while holding the exclusive lock
findings.body: `readWebAssetsFromCDN` (HTTP GET with the request context) and `readWebAssetsFromFile` are executed while the write lock is held, so every other caller of `GetWebAssets` — including readers that would otherwise hit the cache — is blocked for the duration of a network round trip or disk read. In dev mode, where the cache is bypassed on every call, this fully serializes all asset-manifest lookups across requests. Consider loading into a local variable outside the lock and only taking the lock to publish the result.

findings.title: No test exercising concurrent GetWebAssets calls
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test. A simple test that calls `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines (runnable under `-race`), covering both `setting.Dev` and non-dev configs, would prevent regression if the locking is later removed or the global is reintroduced elsewhere.
